title: Categorical valuative invariants of polyhedra and matroids
summary: Six bounded findings: four affect stated core proofs, constructions or an advertised explicit application; two concern local filtration or relaxation boundary statements. Several claims remain true after explicit repairs; the main maximizing-face theorem is not refuted.
limitations: The reviewed object is the pinned arXiv author manuscript, not a verified journal version of record.
All 56 PDF pages were text-read across the root and native helpers; this is not a claim that every proof or cited external theorem was independently reconstructed.
No separate supplement or released repository was available in the acquired manifest; absence of code is not a mathematical defect.
The general augmented proof of Theorem 6.3 has not been repaired; the counterexamples refute printed intermediate claims, not the final theorem.
No independent comprehensive search of later journal corrections or full-text version correspondence was completed.

problems.title: The augmented complex invalidates Lemma6.9 and a step in Theorem6.3
problems.assumptions: Finite face decomposition; P=[0,1], psi(x)=x; trivial subdivision explicitly allowed; F={1} is an internal face of Q_psi.
problems.check: The full augmented complex is P in degrees2 and1 with differential identity. Maximization gives F->F with identity, hence zero homology. Lemma6.9 predicts F[-1], with nonzero degree1 homology. A subdivision of [0,2] at1 gives the same failure in a nontrivial subdivision.
problems.result: Printed auxiliary lemma false; subsequent minimal-complex argument invalid.
problems.counterevidence: The final Theorem6.3 remains true in these examples because both full complexes are contractible. Correcting the order filtration does not remove this one-object counterexample.
problems.impact: Direct dependency into the technical heart and categorical convolution theorem.

correction.statement: Truncate first, then correctly track and restore the augmentation by a cone; the full argument is not supplied as proven.

problems.title: Corollary9.8 uses the wrong exterior degree
problems.assumptions: Gamma trivial, rank2 M=U1,{1,2} direct sum U1,{3}, H={1,2}, h=2; H is a stressed hyperplane.
problems.check: OS dimensions are (1,2,1) before relaxation and (1,3,2) afterwards. Printed wedge^2 of one-dimensional V[1,1] vanishes and predicts zero change; true change is t+t^2.
problems.result: Explicit formula false on fully admissible input.
problems.counterevidence: Lemma9.7 has wedge^(k-1), suggesting a transcription origin but not removing the substantive wrong calculation.
problems.impact: An explicitly advertised equivariant OS application is incorrect as printed.

correction.statement: Replace wedge^k by wedge^(k-1); general propagation follows Lemma9.7 wherever Proposition9.6 is valid. Its separate exceptional proof branch is not thereby repaired.

problems.title: The flag-lifting induction asserts an unsupported intersection rank
problems.assumptions: M=U3,4; M'=U2,{1,2,3} direct sum U1,{4}; target flag {3} subset {1,2,3}; admissible F2={1,2}.
problems.check: Source/target rank F2 is2 and cl_M'(F2)={1,2,3}, but F1' intersect F2 is empty and has rank0, not k1=1.
problems.result: Printed induction step false; the proposition itself is true by the independent repair.
problems.counterevidence: A specially chosen compatible lift works, but the original induction supplied only an arbitrary lift with target closure.
problems.impact: The printed proof supports the emphasized Chow monotonicity/surjectivity result.

correction.statement: Choose nested target bases B_i adapted to the flag and set F_i=cl_M(B_i). Target independence implies source independence. Weak-map rank inequalities imply F_i subset F_i' and cl_M'(F_i)=F_i', including rank0/loops.

problems.title: Lower-set subcomplexes do not isolate an object in the stated order
problems.assumptions: Thin category a<b with unique nonidentity arrow f:a->b; C1=a, C0=b, d=f.
problems.check: C^(<=a)=C^(<b)=0 and C^(<=b)=C, so C^b=C is minimal with nonzero differential, contrary to the asserted necessarily trivial differential.
problems.result: Local filtration construction incorrect as written.
problems.counterevidence: The expected object filtration is obtained by upper sets; this does not refute minimal-complex uniqueness.
problems.impact: Local foundational definition used later; no independent additional core failure is inferred beyond P1.

correction.statement: Use upper-set subcomplexes C^(>=X), C^(>X), or consistently reverse the order convention.

problems.title: Relaxation statements omit orbit and empty-cusp boundary cases

location.claim: Theorems3.8/3.10 and Proposition9.6 exceptional proof branch

problems.assumptions: M=U1,{1,2} direct sum U1,{3,4}; Gamma generated by(13)(24); F={1,2}. Additional case M=U2,3, F={1}.
problems.check: The orbit relaxation adds both12 and34 and yields U2,4, whereas Lambda_F adds only12; the resulting two-pyramid subdivision is not trivial. In the second case cusp is empty and Pi=Lambda is a boundary edge, not an internal cell.
problems.result: Exceptional decomposition classification false in admitted degeneracies.
problems.counterevidence: The subdivision is valid in the orbit example; the virtual representation identity in Proposition9.6 still holds there through Ind Res X=X tensor(1+sgn).
problems.impact: Local boundary classification and cited proof shortcut; no general falsity of Proposition9.6 is established.

correction.statement: Treat singleton-orbit/trivial and complementary orbit cases separately; exclude or explicitly handle empty cusps. No fully general repaired relaxation theorem claimed.

problems.title: Euclidean unit normals need not belong to the rational determinant morphism line
problems.assumptions: Split P(U2,5) by x1+x2=1; the middle cell is P(U1,{1,2} direct sum U1,{3,4,5}), an internal facet.
problems.check: Outward unit normal is ±(3,3,-2,-2,-2)/sqrt30. The rational functional x1+x2 vanishes on the facet direction space and descends to the rational quotient; its value ±6/sqrt30 is irrational, excluding even a rational coset representative.
problems.result: The stated differential is not defined in the specified Q-linear category.
problems.counterevidence: The real construction and intended virtual-character identity are not refuted; arbitrary rational rescaling is not automatically a chain-level repair.
problems.impact: The equivariant categorical construction, a central stated motivation, needs a valid rational differential.

correction.statement: Use outward primitive generators of the saturated quotient lattices L_N/L_N' with L_N=V(N) intersect Z^E. Determinant exact sequences make the two codimension-two composites opposite primitive generators; permutation actions preserve these generators. Compatible lattice volume forms identify the repaired complex with the signed incidence complex.

independent_acceptance_review.performing_role: Current acceptance root; independent focused mathematical verification
independent_acceptance_review.scope: Independent acceptance of all six reported findings, their exact admissible examples, counterevidence, severity, downstream scope and stated repairs. Current root read the entire report, findings and coverage, and the decisive source definitions and proofs. Historical full-paper coverage remains attributed to its actual initial readers; current acceptance does not claim a second complete 56-page reconstruction.

findings.reason: The trivial interval decomposition is expressly admissible (p.10), the augmentation is expressly in degree d+1 (p.17), and the maximizing functor sends its identity differential to identity (p.26). For F={1}, the full objectwise complex is therefore F in degree 2 -> F in degree 1, contractible, while Lemma 6.9 gives F[-1] with nonzero H1. The nontrivial split interval has the same maximizing-block failure. This invalidates the printed central derivation and graded minimal-complex identification. It does not refute Theorem 6.3 itself, since both full complexes in the examples are contractible. The proposed truncated/cone repair remains unproved in general.

For M=U1,{1,2} direct sum U1,{3}, H={1,2} is a stressed rank-one hyperplane and the trivial group is allowed. Circuit-boundary or NBC counts give dimensions (1,2,1) and (1,3,2) after relaxation, so the actual change is t+t^2. The printed wedge^2 of a one-dimensional representation vanishes. Wedge^(k-1) restores this example and follows the preceding lemma, conditionally on the separate relaxation identity. A short exponent edit does not eliminate the false advertised formula's substantive impact.

findings.decision: retain Major with complete local repair
findings.reason: The map U3,4 -> U2,{1,2,3} direct sum U1,{4} has the correct basis-inclusion direction. F2={1,2} is a valid rank-two lift of {1,2,3}, but its intersection with {3} has rank zero. Thus the arbitrary-lift induction is invalid. Adapted nested target bases B_i remain independent in the source; F_i=cl_M B_i has the right rank, and the weak-map rank inequalities force B_i subset F_i subset F_i' and cl_M' F_i=F_i'. This proves surjectivity, including rank-zero loop flats, without an extra hypothesis. The final monotonicity assertion is not refuted.

In the thin a->b category, the maximal subcomplex supported only on a is zero, whereas the one supported on <=b is the full nonzero differential. The asserted object quotient is not an isolated b block. Upper sets are closed under arrows and give the stated local repair. This issue neither refutes uniqueness of minimal complexes nor removes the independent one-object augmentation witness.

The two-block C2 orbit adds both missing bases 12 and 34, while a single relaxation adds only one; the actual two-pyramid subdivision is not trivial. The U2,3 singleton flat has uniform restriction/contraction but empty cusp, putting Pi=Lambda on a boundary edge. Both satisfy the printed definitions. The determinant-twisted identity in the square example nevertheless agrees with Proposition 9.6 through Ind Res V=V tensor(1+sgn). Thus a false boundary classification and proof shortcut are established, not falsity of the general final representation identity.

findings.decision: retain Major with coherent rational repair
findings.reason: The U2,5 split has genuine matroid cells and an internal facet. The proposed unit normal has class +/- (3,3,-2,-2,-2)/sqrt(30); the rational quotient functional delta_H gives +/-6/sqrt(30), excluding any rational representative. Saturated tangent lattices provide outward primitive quotient generators. Their determinant exact sequences identify both codimension-two compositions with opposite primitive generators, so incidence signs cancel; maximal-cell augmentation and permutation equivariance are preserved. This repairs the rational complex coherently, rather than merely dropping 'unit' or allowing arbitrary independent rescalings.
